name: Brachydactyly type A2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and radiographic criteria for Brachydactyly type A2

criteria.description: Shortening or hypoplasia of the middle phalanx of the index finger
Isolated brachydactyly affecting the second digit with normal or near-normal other digits
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Radiographic evidence of middle phalanx shortening and abnormal morphology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of shortening of the middle phalanx of the index finger confirmed radiographically, with or without positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in the IHH gene may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

occasional.symptomName: Short middle phalanx of the 5th finger
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger

imaging: Radiographs showing shortening and hypoplasia of the middle phalanx of the second digit
Normal bone morphology in other digits
genetic: Mutations in the IHH (Indian Hedgehog) gene associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Shortening of middle phalanges of the second, third, and fifth digits
More generalized brachydactyly compared to isolated second digit involvement
Shortening of middle phalanges of multiple digits including the fourth and fifth fingers

redFlags: Progressive worsening of finger deformity beyond early childhood
Presence of systemic abnormalities suggesting syndromic brachydactyly
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
